newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-B.A.T reassures on U.S. tobacco deal.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-B.A.T reassures on U.S. tobacco deal.

text.p: Britain's B.A.T Industries Plc assured investors on Wednesday a landmark settlement of legal claims against the tobacco industry in the United States announced in June was unlikely to affect other countries.

"Shareholders may well be concerned about whether the proposed resolution will also affect other countries. We do not consider that it will," said chairman Lord Cairns in a statement attached to the group's half year results.

But a surprise decision by the group to hold its dividend at the interim and full year stages was due to the cost and uncertainty of the settlement, added Michael Prideaux, head of group public affairs, in an interview.
"It's a case of short term pain for long term gain. The point of all this is that people will now be able to put a value on Brown and Williamson within the group," said Prideaux in an interview.
Brown & Williamson, a subsidiary of B.A.T, is the thirst largest cigarette maker in the United States with brands like Kent, Lucky Strike and Kool.

The decision to hold the dividend at 10 pence per share for the six months to June 30 and leave the final dividend unchanged at no less than last year's 16.0 pence, sent the group's shares 10-1/2p lower to 529p.
Analysts had forecast an increase to between 10.7p and 10.8p per share at the half year stage and a five to eight percent rise in the final dividend.

The group announced pretax profits of 1.247 billion pounds in the six months to June 30, down 64 million or five percent on the first half of 1996, due mainly to the 61 million pounds impact of the strength of sterling.
American tobacco companies agreed with state attorney's in June to settle most legal claims against them in return for payments totalling 230 billion pounds over 25 years.

Under the agreement the industry also accepted tougher regulation of their products and advertising restrictions in return for immunity from most legal claims. The funds raised by the levy will be used to meet Medicaid costs incurred for treating smoking related diseases.
If the settlement terms are approved by Congress B.A.T is obliged to pay $1.7 billion upfront. The second payment into the fund falls due one year after enactment.

"We think it would have been misleading given the short term uncertainty to have carried on as usual," said Prideaux. He said the proposal was under attack from health groups and the timetable for enactment by Congress was slipping.
"We were hopeful it would be enacted by the end of this year but that is now looking less likely," he said, adding there were two important motives for not letting it slip too far.

"First, the $10 billion upfront payment is not payable until the proposals are enacted. Second, the first payment into the fund is not due until the end of the first full year following enactment. So the States who stand to get most of this money for their Medicaid programmes could be waiting until 1999."

Meanwhile, trading profit from tobacco rose six percent to 800 million pounds if the 22 million costs of closing a cigarette factory in Berlin and 21 million for a legal settlement in Mississippi are excluded. The group's total cigarette volumes were flat at 340 billion.

The company reported a strong increase in tobacco sales in the Latin America region, supporting its rationale for the acquisition of Cigarerra La Moderna, the leading cigarette maker in Mexico, for $1.7 billion announced on July 22.

The group's Lucky Strike brand showed strong sales in Germany and Spain while total profits in Europe were 25 million higher at 86 million pounds, reflecting higher cigarette prices, especially in Germany.

In financial services, total trading profit rose six percent to 593 million with good performances from Farmers in the United States, Allied Dunbar in Britain and Canada Trust. Profit from the general business was ahead four percent at 346 million pounds and from the life companies nine percent at 247 million. ($ = 0.613 British Pounds)
